long_biography.plain_text:
Murray Kessler’s experience as an amateur show jumper shaped his approach to running American equestrian sport. With limited family money, he had started at small, one-day shows before competing nationally. As federation president, he wanted participation to remain possible for riders beginning on similarly restricted budgets.

His programme introduced a lower-cost membership for fans, educational videos and Competition Lite events to make recognised competition more accessible. It also expanded member benefits and access to insurance. Membership more than doubled during his term. The changes accompanied stronger support for para-dressage, including a programme to certify coaches, and clearer development routes for young riders.
